birdnetR

Note: This README describes the development version, birdnetR 1.0. It is a breaking release and not on CRAN yet: all functions have new birdnet_<verb> names, and BirdNET+ V3.0 is the default model. CRAN still has 0.3.2, which is documented at https://birdnet-team.github.io/birdnetR/. If you are upgrading from 0.x, see Upgrading from birdnetR 0.x below.

birdnetR brings BirdNET to R. BirdNET is a deep learning model that identifies birds and many other animals by their sounds. birdnetR helps you analyze audio from bioacoustic projects, from a few recordings to large datasets, even without a background in computer science.

birdnetR wraps the birdnet Python package and sets up Python for you. With it you can:

  • identify species in audio files with BirdNET+ V3.0 (the default), BirdNET V2.4 or Google’s Perch v2,
  • predict which species occur at a location and week of the year (geo models),
  • extract embeddings (one feature vector per audio segment) for your own analyses,
  • run custom classifiers trained with BirdNET-Analyzer.

To train custom classifiers, use BirdNET-Analyzer directly.

Installation

Install the development version (1.0) from GitHub:

pak::pak("birdnet-team/birdnetR")

The released version on CRAN is still 0.3.2, with the old function names:

install.packages("birdnetR")

You don’t need to install Python yourself. On first use, birdnetR sets up Python and the birdnet package for you (through reticulate). The first setup takes a few minutes. The default installation is small. TensorFlow (about 600 MB) and PyTorch are downloaded only when you first load a model that needs them.

Installation and setup covers these extra downloads, your own Python environment and working offline. For GPUs, see the GPU article.

Example use

Identify species in an audio file:

library(birdnetR)

# Load the BirdNET+ V3.0 acoustic model (downloaded on first use)
model <- birdnet_load()

# Path to an audio file (replace with your own file path)
audio_path <- system.file("extdata", "soundscape.mp3", package = "birdnetR")

# Predict species in the audio file
predictions <- birdnet_predict(model, audio_path)

# Convert predictions to a data frame
df <- as.data.frame(predictions)

Each row of df is one detection: the file (input), the segment’s start_time and end_time in seconds, the species_name ("<scientific name>_<common name>") and the confidence score.

Other models load the same way:

model_24 <- birdnet_load(version = "2.4")   # BirdNET V2.4
perch <- birdnet_load_perch()               # Google's Perch v2
geo <- birdnet_load(type = "geo")           # species expected at a place and week

Working with prediction results

birdnet_predict() returns a lightweight Python-backed object, not an R data frame. Use as.data.frame() when you need the results in R. For large runs, it is faster to skip the conversion and write the results to a file directly:

predictions <- birdnet_predict(model, audio_path)

# Faster for large runs; the data stays in Python:
birdnet_write(predictions, "results.parquet")

# Only when you need the results in R:
df <- as.data.frame(predictions)

Models

Model Load with Classes License of the model files
BirdNET+ V3.0 acoustic (default) birdnet_load() about 11,700 Apache 2.0
BirdNET+ V3.0 geo birdnet_load(type = "geo") about 14,000 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
BirdNET V2.4 acoustic birdnet_load(version = "2.4") 6,522 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
BirdNET V2.4 geo birdnet_load(type = "geo", version = "2.4") 6,522 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
Perch v2 (Google) birdnet_load_perch() 14,795 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

birdnet_list_models() lists every backend and precision you can choose. The Models and backends article explains them. For details on each model, see the models page of the Python package.

Upgrading from birdnetR 0.x

Version 1.0 is a breaking release. The table below maps removed functions to their replacements:

0.3.2 1.0.0
birdnet_model_tflite() birdnet_load(version = "2.4", backend = "tf")
birdnet_model_protobuf() birdnet_load(version = "2.4", backend = "pb")
birdnet_model_meta() birdnet_load(type = "geo", version = "2.4")
birdnet_model_custom() birdnet_load_custom()
predict_species_from_audio_file() birdnet_predict(model, files = ...)
predict_species_at_location_and_time() birdnet_predict(model, latitude = ..., longitude = ...)
labels_path() / read_labels() birdnet_list_species(model); read your own list file with readLines()
available_languages() birdnet_list_languages()
get_top_prediction() Removed; use dplyr or birdnetTools
install_arrow() Removed; not needed

Predictions now come back as an object (convert with as.data.frame()), and the output columns follow the Python package (input, start_time, end_time, species_name, confidence). NEWS.md lists the renamed arguments and all other changes.

The BirdNET ecosystem

birdnetR is part of a set of related tools:

  • BirdNET-Analyzer — the upstream desktop/CLI application for custom classifier training and advanced BirdNET features.
  • birdnetTools — an R package for post-processing and validating BirdNET predictions: filtering, visualization, and interactive threshold setting.

Citation

Feel free to use birdnetR for your acoustic analyses and research. If you do, please cite as:

@article{kahl2021birdnet,
  title={BirdNET: A deep learning solution for avian diversity monitoring},
  author={Kahl, Stefan and Wood, Connor M and Eibl, Maximilian and Klinck, Holger},
  journal={Ecological Informatics},
  volume={61},
  pages={101236},
  year={2021},
  publisher={Elsevier}
}
